name: 46,XX Testicular Difference of Sex Development

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for 46,XX Testicular DSD

criteria.description: Presence of 46,XX karyotype in an individual with male phenotype
Histological or imaging confirmation of testicular tissue despite 46,XX karyotype
Detection of SRY gene translocation to X chromosome or autosomes or its absence
Presence of male external genitalia with or without hypospadias or cryptorchidism
Elevated testosterone levels with low or normal gonadotropins consistent with testicular function

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: 46,XX karyotype with confirmed testicular tissue and presence or absence of SRY gene translocation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing for SRY and other sex-determining genes is critical for confirmation.

laboratory: Hormonal profile showing normal to elevated testosterone with elevated LH and FSH
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI demonstrating presence of testicular tissue
Absence or hypoplasia of Müllerian structures
other: Histopathological confirmation of testicular tissue if biopsy performed

distinguishingFeatures: Female external genitalia despite male genotype
Normal or elevated testosterone with androgen receptor defects

redFlags: Discordance between chromosomal sex and phenotypic sex
Presence of ambiguous genitalia or hypospadias at birth
Delayed or incomplete puberty with infertility
references: Müller J, et al. 46,XX Testicular DSD: Clinical and Molecular Features. Eur J Endocrinol. 2022;186(3):R1-R14.
Hughes IA, et al. Consensus Statement on Management of Differences of Sex Development. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2021;17(7):415-429.
Orphanet Report Series: 46,XX Testicular Difference of Sex Development. Orphanet. 2023.
